<p class="theme-lead">Many of society's logistics problems — collecting waste, gritting roads, delivering parcels, allocating cloud resources — are <b>combinatorial optimisation</b> problems: the number of possible solutions explodes with problem size. I design <b>evolutionary and memetic algorithms</b> that find near-optimal solutions quickly, and <b>decomposition</b> methods that let them scale to problems with thousands of decisions.</p>

<a name="introduction"></a>
<h2>Introduction</h2>
<h3>The problems</h3>
<p>In the <b>capacitated arc routing problem (CARP)</b>, a fleet of vehicles with limited capacity must serve a set of streets — for example to collect waste — at minimum total cost. Related problems include vehicle routing with electric vehicles or drones, team orienteering, job shop scheduling and service allocation. They are NP-hard, so exact methods quickly become impractical.</p>

<h3>Why evolutionary computation?</h3>
<p>Evolutionary algorithms search with a <i>population</i> of solutions, recombining good ones. <b>Memetic algorithms</b> add problem-specific local search, combining global exploration with powerful local refinement. They handle complex constraints and multiple objectives naturally and give good solutions within practical time.</p>
<figure class="theme-figure">
<svg class="theme-svg" viewBox="0 0 720 225" role="img" aria-label="Memetic algorithm"><title>Memetic algorithm</title><desc>Evolutionary search combined with problem-specific local search.</desc><defs><marker id="arr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" class="svg-arrowhead"/></marker></defs><rect x="20" y="40" width="170" height="60" rx="6" class="svg-box"/><text y="66.5" text-anchor="middle" class="svg-label"><tspan x="105.0" dy="0">Population of</tspan><tspan x="105.0" dy="17">candidate solutions</tspan></text><rect x="270" y="40" width="170" height="60" rx="6" class="svg-box"/><text y="66.5" text-anchor="middle" class="svg-label"><tspan x="355.0" dy="0">Crossover</tspan><tspan x="355.0" dy="17">(recombine routes)</tspan></text><rect x="520" y="40" width="180" height="60" rx="6" class="svg-box svg-box--accent"/><text y="66.5" text-anchor="middle" class="svg-label"><tspan x="610.0" dy="0">Local search</tspan><tspan x="610.0" dy="17">e.g. Merge-Split operator</tspan></text><rect x="270" y="150" width="170" height="60" rx="6" class="svg-box"/><text y="176.5" text-anchor="middle" class="svg-label"><tspan x="355.0" dy="0">Selection &amp;</tspan><tspan x="355.0" dy="17">replacement</tspan></text><path d="M190,70 L266,70" class="svg-arrow" marker-end="url(#arr)"/><path d="M440,70 L516,70" class="svg-arrow" marker-end="url(#arr)"/><path d="M610,100 Q610,180 444,180" class="svg-arrow" marker-end="url(#arr)"/><path d="M270,180 Q105,180 105,104" class="svg-arrow" marker-end="url(#arr)"/></svg>

<h2>My Contributions</h2>
<p>With my students and collaborators, I have made the following contributions. The papers shown are selected automatically: award-winning papers, papers with 100+ citations, and papers in top venues. Click a title to read the paper, or <i>list entry</i> to see it in my publication list.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">1</span> Memetic algorithms for arc routing</h3>
<p>We proposed MAENS, whose Merge-Split operator explores far beyond traditional local moves and became a widely used benchmark, and extended memetic search to multi-objective, periodic and uncertain arc routing.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">2</span> Large-scale optimisation by decomposition</h3>
<p>Very large problems are solved by splitting them into smaller interacting sub-problems. Our <b>differential grouping</b> detects variable interactions automatically, and <b>route distance grouping</b> and route clustering decompose large arc routing problems.</p>
